newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes drift up at close on thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes drift up at close on thin volume.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed up 10 basis points at 29.20 percent on Thursday after zigzagging during what traders described as a listless session.
"Trade was very light again. A market with volume this thin lends itself to sharp rises and falls in rates," said a trader.
The overnight rate earlier reached a high of 30.00 percent during the session.
Banco de Mexico injected 4.650 billion pesos by auctioning four credits which it assigned at between 31.39 and 32.19 percent.

Liquidity shortages had originally been estimated at 2.502 billion pesos due to credit maturities, and to be eased by a surplus from the primary Cetes auction. More liquidity was drained from the system, however, prior to the weekend and to meet first-half Novemnber payroll expenses.

"There was a surplus carried over from the primary auction, but demand for cash was very heavy. There was demand for payrolls, for the weekend and probably the November 20 holiday, too," a trader said.
Traders estimated total credit maturities at 3.853 billion pesos for Friday.
